exercise1.prompt: Choosing a Chart: The table behind a bar chart

hiddenCases.name: each bar is its own team's mean
the summary is computed, not typed

exercise1.hint: A bar chart of "mean by team" is a group-by with the means rounded for display. Get that table right and the chart is one more line.

exercise2.prompt: Choosing a Chart: Bars in a readable order

hiddenCases.name: the order is by value, not by name
the summary is computed, not typed

exercise2.hint: Group to a mean per team, round, sort_values(ascending=False), then build plain (name, value) tuples with str() and float().

questions.prompt: Which chart suits comparing one value across a handful of categories?
questions.explain: Bars share a baseline and encode value as length, which people compare most accurately.

questions.prompt: Which suits the distribution of a single numeric column?
questions.explain: It answers "what do the values look like", which no summary statistic does on its own.

questions.prompt: Why is a pie chart usually the wrong choice?
choices: Angle is read less accurately than length, and it only shows parts of one whole
questions.explain: Any comparison it makes, a bar chart makes more precisely.

questions.prompt: When should bars NOT be sorted by value?
choices: When the category has a natural order, like months
When there are more than five
questions.explain: Sorting months by value destroys the thing the reader is using to navigate.
